thread:
anya: Kicking off the runtime roadmap Q&A — thanks for coming. Drop any questions about performance, batching, kernels, or rollout plans and we'll answer live.

sam: Quick one — what's the ETA on the new continuous-batching prototype landing in prod?

anya: Sam will take this. We're aiming for canary in mid-May, GA end of Q2, assuming no major regressions. Depends on infra validation and perf numbers.

sam: Cool. Specific perf targets?

liam: Target is 20–30% throughput improvement for multi-tenant workloads at 1kQPS and p99 latency <= 120ms on our p4-like hosts. Those are measured with mixed short/long seq distributions.

nadia: Are we confident the KV cache changes won't increase memory pressure on smaller instances? We saw an OOM in last week's lab run.

sam: Good call. The prototype introduces an adaptive expiration policy to bound KV memory by per-worker quota. We also added an eviction priority that favors longer-lived prefixes. The OOM you saw was due to a missed quota check — that's fixed in the next patch.

matt: How will this affect downstream latency spikes (the sawtooth behavior we've been seeing under bursty traffic)?

liam: Continuous batching smooths token emission by packing partially-filled batches instead of waiting for timers. For bursty traffic it should reduce p99 spikes because more requests are batched quickly. There's a slight p50 increase in some microbenchmarks due to packing overhead (~2–5ms) but net p99 wins.

anya: We should be explicit about tradeoffs in the release notes. Sam, can you add a short blurb about the p50/p99 tradeoffs and recommended config toggles for latency-sensitive apps?

sam: Yep. I'll include recommended `max_batch_latency_ms`, `min_batch_size`, and `kv_mem_quota` examples. Example snippet:```json
{
  "max_batch_latency_ms": 10,
  "min_batch_size": 4,
  "kv_mem_quota": "6GB"
}
```

nadia: Nice. On kernels — any progress upstreaming the fused attention kernels? Licensing was a blocker last cycle.

liam: We resolved the license issue with the kernel contributor. The fused kernels are in an internal branch now; integration tests are green except for a GPU codegen corner case on Ampere that we need to investigate. If that stays small, we can flip it behind a feature flag for Dedicated first.

matt: Can Dedicated customers opt into the new kernels independently of Hosted? We had asks for isolating risk.

anya: Yes. Deployment model allows per-cluster flags. Dedicated clusters can opt-in while Hosted stays on the safe path until we've ramped.

sam: Ops question — what telemetry will we expose to customers to help them decide to opt-in?

liam: We'll add per-route throughput/cost deltas, kernel version tag, and p50/p99 deltas in the Console. Also an A/B rollout helper in Optimize to simulate cost impact against historical traces.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout job queued for cluster 'canary-3' — ETA 45m.

nadia: One more: regression alerts — are we tying eval sets to rollout so we can auto-rollback on quality drops?

sam: Yes — rollouts will include optional eval hooks. If the eval fails threshold, the controller will pause and notify the runbook channel. We're piloting with the summarization and instruction-following evals first.

matt: How are we communicating SLO changes to customers? This is a common ask.

anya: We'll update the SLO page and add a migration guide: what opt-ins do to latency/cost and recommended knobs. Customer success will run a few webinars.

liam: FYI — kernel team discovered a 7% perf regression for very short sequences with quantized kernels. Working on a microkernel tweak, should be next week.

sam: Thanks. If anyone wants to dig into the canary logs tonight ping me — I'll be watching the rollout and the tracing spans for batching efficiency.

anya: Great. If there are no more questions, we'll pause here. I'll post a short follow-up with links to the canary dashboard, rollout playbook, and the config gist. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
